name: What flooring is safest for an accessible bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Which bathroom flooring materials offer the best slip resistance without looking cheap or dated?
mainEntity.text: Which bathroom flooring materials offer the best slip resistance without looking cheap or dated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom flooring for accessibility should prioritize traction, moisture resistance, and easy maintenance. Slip-resistant porcelain tile is a common choice because it performs well in wet conditions and comes in many styles that fit both modern and traditional homes. Smaller-format tile can sometimes improve grip because of the extra grout lines, while very glossy finishes tend to be less forgiving. Luxury vinyl or other resilient materials may work in some areas, but the contractor should confirm they are suitable for wet rooms and compatible with the shower transition. The safest floor is one that reduces fall risk without creating a bumpy or hard-to-clean surface. Homeowners should also think about color contrast, because visible edge definition can help users with low vision navigate the space more confidently.
acceptedAnswer.description: The safest accessible bathroom flooring is usually slip-resistant tile or another hard surface with enough traction when wet. The best choice balances grip, durability, and easy cleaning while avoiding glossy finishes that become slick around showers and sinks.
